This is the two-controls-writing-independently failure the week stepper comment above it exists to prevent.

cases.why: the select ships visually-hidden, which is the tidy-up a reader makes on seeing enhanceSelect hide it anyway -- and it matches what the week stepper's markup does, so it looks like consistency. What it costs is ordering: the select is then hidden before the listbox that replaces it is built, so a script that dies in between leaves the Week Board with no sort control instead of a working native one. Nothing errors and the rendered page is identical for everyone else. CORRECTED 2026-09-21: this entry used to say the loss was a no-script reader's only control. That reader cannot reach this page -- with scripts off only #page-ratings is active and every nav control is an inert <button> -- so the honest cost is the ordering property, not reach.

enhanceSelect is called one line earlier, above the change listener rather than below it. The control renders correctly, opens, highlights, closes and shows the chosen label -- and the board never re-sorts, because the change it dispatches reaches a listener that does not exist yet. Every visual check passes; only sorting is dead.

the Space arm stops asking whether a search is in flight. This is the defect that shipped in the first working build and that no amount of source reading found: the first space typed selects whatever is under the cursor and closes the list, so type-ahead can never reach an option past its first word. Re-measured on the built page after the "Sort: " prefix was dropped, because the original example rested on a shared prefix that no longer exists: typing "biggest s" walks the active option to "Biggest Spread First" as shipped, and with this mutation applied the space chooses "Biggest Model Disagreement" and closes the list instead.

the list stops publishing which option the keyboard is on. Sighted keyboard users still see .is-active move, every behavioural check still passes, and a screen-reader user hears nothing as they arrow through the list -- the option under the cursor is simply never announced. It is the piece most often dropped because it is the one with no visual consequence.

the chevron stops inheriting and takes .week-select's exact stroke colour. In dark mode it is indistinguishable from correct. In light mode it is a dark-theme grey on a white surface, on the one chevron anybody actually sees. CORRECTED 2026-09-21 on two counts: .week-select's own chevron is not a live instance of this defect, because every element wearing that class is clipped to 1x1 and it never paints; and the deferral to "Stage 11" named a stage that has never existed in this project. teamColor()'s fallback is the real sibling, and it is queued under Stage 9.

one padding goes back to a hardcoded pair. It is exactly the change that feels harmless while nudging a control's height, and it is how .week-select accumulated the 31 ad-hoc spacing values Stage 8 exists to answer. A new component is where retired scales come back, one declaration at a time, each with a good local reason.

The listbox button then goes on naming whatever team it last rendered, directly above an empty state saying there is no data. the assignment goes and the call stays. This is the mutation that was written before the guard that catches it, and it walked through every other test in the file: the listbox is still built, still correct on load, `enhanceSelect(` is still there for the coverage test and the literal `refresh()` is still there for the branch test. Only the thing that would call it is gone. It is the exact shape of a guard whose comment claims more than its code delivers, which this repository has now shipped five times.

the aria-label goes. Sighted use is completely unchanged, because the button's visible text is the selected team either way. To a screen reader the control announces as a bare button with no name, which is strictly less than the native select it replaced -- and there is no visible label anywhere near it to fall back on, only the page's own h2.

the same tidy-up as the sort-select case above, applied to the select that needs it even more: this one has no options in the markup either, so hiding it there hides it before either its options or its listbox exist. the sentinel stops asking the select and starts asking the listbox. It works on load and reads as the more direct question, but it moves the answer to "does this page have teams yet" out of the element that owns them and into a control that is supposed to be invisible to everything downstream of it. Two sources of truth for one piece of state, which is the contract this component was built to avoid.

a THIRD write to the options appears, and neither existing branch is touched -- the no-data branch still refreshes and the populate branch still enhances, so both of the case-shaped guards above stay green. This is the case the coverage test exists for rather than a specific edit anyone is expected to make: the guard enumerates the writes precisely because the next one will be added by someone who checked that the two they knew about were handled. CLAUDE.md records the shape as prose naming a protection but never its coverage.
